q: A bomb calorimeter is used to measure the energy content of ____. (2024)
e: A bomb calorimeter is a device used to measure the heat released during combustion to determine the energy content of fuels.

q: The neutralisation reaction is exothermic and the enthalpy change is ____. (2025)
e: Exothermic reactions release heat to the surroundings, resulting in a negative enthalpy change.

q: Plants store ____ in carbohydrates formed during photosynthesis. (2025)
e: Solar energy absorbed by plants during photosynthesis is converted and stored as chemical energy.

q: Plants store chemical energy in ____ formed during photosynthesis. (2025)
e: Carbohydrates synthesized during photosynthesis act as the storage medium for chemical energy.

q: ____ is used to measure the energy content of fuels. (2026)
e: A bomb calorimeter measures the heat generated by the complete combustion of a fuel sample.

q: The energy needed to make or break bonds is called ____. (2024)
e: Bond enthalpy or bond energy is the measure of bond strength in a chemical bond.

q: The enthalpy changes for the combustion reactions are always ____. (2025)
e: Combustion reactions always release energy into the environment, giving them negative enthalpy values.

q: Heat changes can be measured by using a ____. (2025)
e: A calorimeter is an instrument used to measure heat flow associated with physical or chemical changes.

q: Chemical reactions provide electricity which is the result of ____ between ions in an electrolyte. (2025)
e: Interactions between mobile ions in an electrolyte during redox reactions produce an electric current.

q: When an instant cold pack and a hot pack have been activated, the change in ____ occurs. (2025)
e: The activation of heat and cold packs causes energy transfer that produces a noticeable change in temperature.

q: The standard enthalpy changes of the reaction can be symbolised as ____. (2025)
e: The symbol ΔH° denotes standard enthalpy change measured under standard reference conditions.

q: The symbol for enthalpy change of solution of a substance is ____. (2025)
e: The enthalpy change when a substance dissolves in a solvent is denoted as ΔH_sol.

q: Plants store ____ energy in carbohydrates formed during photosynthesis. (2025)
e: Photosynthesis stores radiant light energy as chemical energy within the bonds of carbohydrates.

q: Non-spontaneous processes need the ____ to take place. (2025)
e: Non-spontaneous processes require a constant supply of external energy to proceed.

q: The enthalpy cycle can be constructed in ____ steps. (2026)
e: Constructing a standard thermochemical enthalpy cycle involves four core operational steps.

q: Combustion reactions are always ____ process. (2025)
e: Combustion always releases heat, making it an exothermic process.

q: The energy needed to make or break bonds is called bond ____. (2025)
e: Bond energy or bond enthalpy quantifies the energy required to break or form chemical bonds.

q: The symbol for bond enthalpy is ____. (2026)
e: The letter E is standard notation used to represent bond enthalpy.

q: The most stable form of carbon is ____. (2025)
e: Graphite is the thermodynamically stable allotrope of carbon under standard conditions.

q: When the ice melts at room temperature, that is a spontaneous and ____ process. (2025)
e: Melting ice absorbs heat from its surroundings (endothermic) and occurs naturally above 0°C (spontaneous).

q: In batteries, chemical reactions provide electricity which is the result of interactions between ____ in an electrolyte. (2026)
e: Batteries convert chemical energy to electrical energy through reactions involving ions in the electrolyte.

q: In a solar cell, energy is transformed from light energy into ____ energy. (2026)
e: Photovoltaic cells transform light energy directly into electrical energy.
